name: Pianoteq
tagline: Physically modelled acoustic and electric piano instrument, available standalone and as a plugin.

pricing.basis: perpetual license, tiered by feature set
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Physical modelling sounds like the kind of thing you can one-shot because there is no sample library to steal, just equations. That is exactly backwards: the equations are the product, and Modartt has been tuning them for close to two decades. An agent will happily give you a bank of modal resonators with hammer noise and a sympathetic resonance toggle, and it will sound like a struck metal object, not a Steinway. The gap between a working string model and one that behaves musically across 88 notes, every velocity layer, half pedal, and release behaviour is thousands of hours of listening and parameter fitting that nobody has written down. You can build the architecture in a day and still be years from something you would record with.
coreLoopDIY: A browser based AudioWorklet instrument that drives per note banks of tuned resonators with a hammer impulse, playable over Web MIDI, so you can hear what raw modal synthesis actually sounds like.
requirements: A Chromium based browser for Web MIDI and AudioWorklet
A MIDI keyboard, ideally with a usable velocity curve
Enough DSP patience to accept that version one sounds like a xylophone
whatYouLose: Two decades of hand tuned per note model parameters across the full keyboard
Credible pedal behaviour: half pedal, sostenuto, release samples, una corda
The instrument library, electric pianos, harpsichords, historical pianos, vibes
Plugin formats, DAW integration, sample accurate automation, low latency native performance
Microphone positioning, cabinet and room models, and the mixing layer that makes it sit in a track
moatNotes: The moat is not code secrecy, the method is published. It is the fitted parameters and the ears that fitted them.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a piano is the single most scrutinised sound in recorded music and everyone can hear when it is wrong. Pianoteq is bought by people who need something that responds correctly at pianissimo, holds up under a close mic, and loads in 50 MB instead of 50 GB. None of that is a feature list you can reimplement, it is the accumulated result of someone comparing model output against real instruments for years. The perpetual license also removes the usual subscription argument: you buy it once and it keeps working.
notes: The architecture of a physical model is a weekend; the parameters are not. The moat is roughly twenty years of someone tuning resonator coefficients by ear against real pianos, and that work exists nowhere except in their binary.
prompt:
Build a browser based physically modelled piano in an empty folder. No frameworks, no build step, no accounts, no telemetry.

Stack: plain HTML, CSS, and ES modules, served by `python3 -m http.server`. Audio via Web Audio API with a single AudioWorkletProcessor. MIDI via Web MIDI API.

What to build:
- index.html with a minimal dark UI: a clickable 88 key keyboard, a MIDI input device selector, a master gain slider, and sliders for hammer hardness, string decay, inharmonicity, and sympathetic resonance amount.
- worklet/piano-processor.js implementing modal synthesis: each active note is a bank of 12 to 20 parallel resonant filters (two pole bandpass or a direct modal state variable), with partial frequencies derived as f * n * sqrt(1 + B * n * n) where B is the inharmonicity coefficient, scaled by note number so bass notes are more inharmonic.
- Excitation: a short noise burst shaped by an exponential envelope whose length and brightness are driven by velocity and the hammer hardness control. Higher velocity means shorter, brighter contact.
- Per partial decay times that shorten with partial index and with pitch, so the top octave dies fast and the bass rings.
- A damper model: note off applies a fast decay ramp unless the sustain pedal (CC64) is held.
- Sympathetic resonance: a shared bank of 6 undamped resonators fed a scaled sum of all active voices, mixed back in at the amount set by the slider. Crude on purpose.
- 32 voice polyphony with oldest voice stealing.
- A soundboard stage: a fixed convolution free approximation using two biquads in series plus a mild waveshaper, nothing fancy.

Out of scope: VST or AU export, sample loading, presets beyond three hardcoded ones, recording, mobile layout, any server side code, any network calls.

Include a README.md that says plainly: this demonstrates the architecture of a modelled piano and will not sound like a real one, and that the gap is parameter tuning, not missing features. List which constants to tweak first.
